consultation.default: Send two to four pages carrying one quotable finding and one discrete recommendation, and submit under an organization name, because organizations get named in the What We Heard report and individuals get aggregated. File a week before the close rather than on the last day, and send the same note to the responsible Director General so a named person has read it. The mistake is sending the paper: analysts need the implication for the options, not the methods section.
consultation.3: Bring a costed ask in the government's own vocabulary and three recommendations, each one sentence. The Department of Finance consultation takes letters or papers with no word limit; the Finance committee's separate pre-budget call caps you at 2,000 words including graphs, footnotes and quotes. Submit to both, before the close, because neither has a late channel. The mistake is treating them as one process.
consultation.5: A consultation at implementation is about delivery, not the problem. Send evidence on what works, for whom, at what cost, and propose one indicator with a named data source. Reach the program Director General through GEDS alongside the form. The mistake is re-arguing the policy: the guidelines are the policy now.

bill.default: Write to a clause, not to the bill. Ten pages maximum to the committee clerk, unlocked with no password, your name on the cover and contact details only in the covering email. Send as early as the study allows, because briefs reach members only once both official languages exist and late means undistributed. The mistake is arguing against the whole bill: the principle was already voted at second reading.
bill.6: A bill that reopens a reviewed program is your chance to fix what the evaluation found. Anchor every recommendation to a published finding, name the report and the page, and give the wording you want changed. Send it to the clerk before clause-by-clause and to the Senate committee separately, because House briefs are not transferred. The mistake is repeating the review instead of translating it into a clause.

gazette.default: Read the Regulatory Impact Analysis Statement first, pick one claim in it to challenge with evidence, and offer alternative wording or a different threshold. Comment at gazette.gc.ca/consult inside the window: 30 days from the Saturday of publication, or at least 70 days where international trade is affected. Everything you send is published under your organization's name for ten years, so write it to be quoted. The mistake is commenting on the policy in general when the department is only answering for the proposal in front of it.
gazette.5: Where a regulation is already in force, the live document is the guidance, not the Gazette notice. Send the department's regulatory team a marked-up passage of the guidance with the operational problem it creates and the evidence behind that. Ask who owns the next review of the instrument. The mistake is waiting for a Part I window that may never reopen.

tender.default: A federal research tender was written by a policy shop that already knows what it is missing, so read the statement of work for the question behind it. Bid on CanadaBuys before the stated closing hour, which is an hour on a day, not the end of that day. If you cannot bid in time, contact the technical authority named in the notice and offer the evidence anyway. The mistake is finding the tender in its closing week: watch the department's Forward Regulatory Plan and Departmental Plan for what is coming.
tender.5: At implementation the requirement is usually a pilot, an evaluation or a guidance product, so lead with capacity to deliver on a government timeline and with ethics approval and data agreements already in place. Name your federal partner if you have one. The mistake is proposing new research when the department is buying an answer it can use inside this fiscal year.

committee.default: Send the clerk a brief of ten pages maximum, unlocked, with a 500-word summary if you run longer, and put your contact details in the covering email rather than on the cover page. Email the clerk separately to say you are available as a witness, naming your specific expertise on that study. Do it early, because committees build witness lists at the start of a study and briefs reach members only once both official languages exist. The mistake is stopping at 2,000 words: that is the Finance committee's pre-budget rule and nobody else's.
committee.1: A study with no bill attached is still being scoped, so the openings are the scope and the witness list. Send the clerk a one-page problem statement, a suggested angle and three witnesses you would recommend, before the first meeting. Senate committees accept self-nomination and are the higher-yield chamber if you have no political sponsor. The mistake is waiting for a call for submissions, because a self-initiated study rarely issues one.
committee.4: Argue one clause. Give the committee the wording you want, a one-paragraph rationale, and the member or senator who will move it, before clause-by-clause begins. The Library of Parliament's Legislative Summary shows how analysts framed each clause, so write your amendment in that frame. The mistake is a locked PDF: password protection blocks the free translation both chambers provide, and untranslated means undistributed.
committee.6: The brief mechanics are unchanged but the timing is not: the review date was public the day the Act passed, so work back twelve months. Committee analysts start from published, findable evidence, so publish first, ask the clerk which analyst is assigned, and send them your work directly. Bring outcome evidence, comparative evidence from other jurisdictions and a short what-to-change list. The mistake is waiting for the review to be announced.

funding.default: A call whose theme was set with a department tells you what that department is about to decide, so read it as intelligence even if you do not apply. Register in the agency portal early: most Tri-agency deadlines close at 8 p.m. eastern and institutional sign-off takes days. Ask your research office for the internal deadline, which is always earlier than the agency's. The mistake is treating the call as separate from the policy file it came out of.
funding.2: A synthesis or partnership call on a named theme means a policy shop is drafting options on that theme. Apply if you can, and either way contact the department that co-set the theme and offer the evidence directly, because the consultation on it has not opened yet. The mistake is waiting for the grant result before making contact.
funding.5: At implementation the money is for co-design, pilots and evaluation, so lead with a named federal partner and with capacity to deliver on a government timeline. Have ethics approval and data-sharing agreements ready before you apply, not after. The mistake is applying without the partner letter, which is the piece that cannot be assembled in the last week.

appointment.default: A body is most open between announcement and appointment. Send the sponsoring minister's office and the responsible department a one-page case for the expertise the body will otherwise be missing, and name two or three other people who should be on it, because recommending reads as more credible than volunteering. Governor in Council opportunities are posted with their own closing dates on the appointments site. The mistake is waiting for a public call, since many advisory bodies are filled by invitation.
appointment.5: Program advisory, technical and standards committees get struck as a program is built, and they fill early and stay filled. Find the program Director General in GEDS and ask one question: who advises you on design. Offer an implementation question you can help answer rather than a research agenda. The mistake is arriving after the first cohort is seated.

review.default: Reviews run on a published calendar, so find the date first: the review clause in the Act, the department's published evaluation plan, or the Auditor General's announced audits. Send the department's Head of Evaluation your outcome and cost evidence about a year before the evaluation starts, with a stated willingness to share data under agreement. On environment and sustainability files anyone may file an environmental petition, and the responsible minister must reply within 120 days. The mistake is arriving with problem evidence when a review needs outcome evidence.
review.1: A completed review is an agenda-setting document with a government response attached, so use it as the opening. Take one recommendation the government accepted, show what has and has not moved since, and take that to the committee that owns the file and to the minister's office. The mistake is reading the review as a conclusion rather than as the moment the file goes back to stage one.
